title: Degree growth conjecture for homogeneous Gaussian cycle polynomials
statement:

title: Extremal-value conjecture for irredundant families when n equals 2k minus 1
statement:
Let $M(n,k)$ be the maximum size of an irredundant family of $k$-dimensional subcubes of $Q_n=\{0,1\}^n$. Let $O$ be the centre vertex used in the source, and let $\mathcal F_O$ be the family of all $k$-subcubes through $O$. For $n=2k-1$, **extremal-value conjecture.**

$$
M(2k-1,k)={2k-1 \choose k}.
$$

The conjectured extremal family is $\mathcal F_O$, whose size is the displayed binomial coefficient. This is the boundary case relevant to the Aharoni–Holzman problem, since a projection argument reduces the general conjecture to $n=2k-1$; the source presents the equality as conjectural.
source_name: David Ellis, “Irredundant Families of Subcubes”, arXiv:1003.2960 (2010).

title: Erdős–Shelah conjecture for maximum union-free subfamilies
statement:
Let $f(m)$ denote the largest integer such that every family of $m$ sets contains a union-free subfamily of size at least $f(m)$, where a family is **union-free** if it has no three distinct sets $X,Y,Z$ with $X\cup Y=Z$. Erdős and Shelah proved the upper bound $f(m)<2\sqrt{m}+1$ and conjectured that it is asymptotically tight.

**Erdős–Shelah conjecture.**

$$
f(m)=(2-o(1))\sqrt{m}.
$$

The paper states that it verifies this conjecture and later proves the exact formula $f(m)=\lfloor\sqrt{4m+1}\rfloor-1$, so the conjecture is solved.
source_name: Jacob Fox, Choongbum Lee and Benny Sudakov, “Maximum union-free subfamilies”, arXiv:1012.3127 (2011).
reason: Primary Theorem 1.2 explicitly gives f(m)=floor(sqrt(4m+1))-1 and says it verifies the conjecture. Contradictory database open note cannot justify rediscovery.

title: Minimum determinant conjecture for bivariate Bézier matrix submatrices
statement:
Let $d$ be a nonnegative integer, let $\mathcal I_d$ be the set of weak $3$-compositions of $d$, and let $N_\Gamma$ be the matrix considered in the paper for a nonempty subset $\Gamma\subset\mathcal I_d$. For $\ell\in\mathbb N$, define

$$
n_d:=\begin{cases}\ell^{3\ell},&d=3\ell,\\(\ell+1)^{\ell+1}\ell^{2\ell},&d=3\ell+1,\\(\ell+1)^{2\ell+2}\ell^\ell,&d=3\ell+2.\end{cases}
$$

**Exact minimum conjecture.**

$$
\min_{\substack{\Gamma\subset\mathcal I_d\\Gamma\neq\emptyset}}\det N_\Gamma=n_d.
$$

This gives a proposed closed form for the smallest determinant among the matrices $N_\Gamma$, refining the determinant-minimization problem. The supplied text does not establish its status.

reason: Primary Conjecture 6 is verified there for d<=7 and Proposition 8 proves |Gamma|<=2. Larger finite minors or singleton optimization are already covered helpers; arbitrary subset determinant lower bounds remain substantial.

title: Conjecture on the exact value of the weighted Hajnal–Szemerédi threshold
statement:

$$
\delta(r,t)=\frac{1}{r}+\left(1-\frac{1}{r}\right)t.

The paper introduces this function and proves matching lower and upper bounds only in special or approximate forms, so the asserted exact formula remains open in the source.

title: The crossing-number conjecture for the crown graph
statement:
Let $K_{n,n}-nK_2$ be the bipartite graph obtained from the complete bipartite graph $K_{n,n}$ by deleting a perfect matching, and let $cr(G)$ denote the crossing number of a graph $G$.

**Crossing-number conjecture.**

$$
cr(K_{n,n}-nK_2)=\left\lfloor\frac{n}{2}\right\rfloor\left\lfloor\frac{n-1}{2}\right\rfloor\left\lfloor\frac{n-2}{2}\right\rfloor\left\lfloor\frac{n-3}{2}\right\rfloor.
$$

This conjecture gives an exact formula for the crossing number of the crown graph. The paper establishes matching upper and substantially weaker lower bounds in general, and proves the formula for $n=5$; the general equality remains open in the supplied text.
source_name: Yuansheng Yang, Baigong Zheng, Xiaohui Lin and Xirong Xu, “The crossing numbers of K_n,n-nK_2, K_nP_2, K_nP_3 and K_nC_4”, arXiv:1211.4437 (2012).

title: Sills–Wang characteristic-polynomial conjecture for the Wiener-index matrix
statement:
Let $A_k=(a_{ij})$ be the $k\times k$ matrix with $a_{ij}=\frac{1}{2}|i-j|$, and let $I_k$ be the $k\times k$ identity matrix. Define $C_k(\lambda)=\det(A_k-\lambda I_k)$ to be the characteristic polynomial of $A_k$. **Sills–Wang's characteristic-polynomial conjecture.**

$$
C_k(\lambda)=(-1)^k\lambda^k\left(1-\frac{k}{4}\sum_{j=1}^{k-1}\frac{j}{j+1}\binom{k+j}{2j+1}\lambda^{-j-1}\right).
$$

The formula gives an explicit expression for the characteristic polynomial and was proposed to obtain sharper information about the largest eigenvalue of $A_k$. The paper proves this conjecture, so its database status is solved.
source_name: Ya-Lei Jin and Xiao-Dong Zhang, “On the Two Conjectures of the Wiener Index”, arXiv:1304.0873 (2013).
reason: Primary Theorem 2.2 proves precisely the displayed characteristic polynomial by scaling the path distance matrix and applying Lemma 2.1. Proof section read; no independent dependency audit.

title: The conjecture on the complementary bounding function of the almost identity function
statement:
Let $g$ be the almost identity function

$$
g(x)=\begin{cases}
3 & \text{for } x=2,\\
x & \text{for } x>2.
\end{cases}
$$

For a graph $G$, let $\alpha(G)$ be its independence number and let $\theta(G)$ be its minimum clique-cover number. The complementary bounding function $g^*$ is the optimal function bounding $\theta(G)$ in terms of $\alpha(G)$ for graphs whose chromatic number is bounded by $g(\omega(G))$. **The conjecture on $g^*$.**

$$
g^*(x)=\left\lfloor\frac{8}{5}x\right\rfloor.
$$

The statement is suggested by the preceding upper bound and is presented as a conjectural formula; the supplied text gives no resolution, so it is recorded as open.
source_name: András Gyárfás, Zhentao Li, Raphael Machado, András Sebo, Stéphan Thomassé and Nicolas Trotignon, “Complements of nearly perfect graphs”, arXiv:1304.2862 (2013).

title: Characterization of inner products by phase covariance
statement:
Let $(X,\|\cdot\|)$ be a complex normed space, and let $\langle\cdot\mid\cdot\rangle$ denote the product induced by the norm through the polarization formula. For every phase $e^{{\bf i}\cdot\varphi}$ on the complex unit circle and all $\vec x,\vec y\in X$, consider the covariance identity

$$
\left\langle e^{{\bf i}\cdot\varphi}\cdot\vec x\mid\vec y\right\rangle=e^{{\bf i}\cdot\varphi}\cdot\left\langle\vec x\mid\vec y\right\rangle.
$$

**Phase-covariance characterization.** This identity holds for all $\vec x,\vec y\in X$ if and only if the product $\langle\cdot\mid\cdot\rangle$ is an inner product, so that $(X,\langle\cdot\mid\cdot\rangle)$ is an inner-product space. The claim would characterize inner-product spaces by the expected complex homogeneity of the induced product. The source gives a counterexample showing that the identity can fail in the supremum norm, but does not establish the stated equivalence in general.
source_name: Volker W. Thürey, “The Complex Angle in Normed Spaces”, arXiv:1308.5412 (2013).
reason: Primary Definition 1.1 normalizes both vectors before polarization. Lemma 3.21 already supplies a supremum-norm failure; it does not refute the iff. Conjecture 3.22 needs phase covariance for every pair and phase to force additivity. Ordinary unnormalized Jordan-von Neumann polarization cannot be substituted.

title: Anand's conjecture on minimizers of the nonlocal strain-gradient plasticity energy
statement:
Let $\ell$ and $h$ be the material length-scale and specimen height, respectively, and let $\mathcal{T}(f)$ be the energy functional

$$
\mathcal{T}(f):=\frac{S_0}{h}\int_0^h\sqrt{f(y)^2+\ell^2|f_{,y}(y)|^2}\,\mathrm{d}y.
$$

Let the space of admissible functions, the yield strength $\tau$, and Equation~ be as specified in the paper. **Anand's conjecture.** The energy $\mathcal{T}$ has a minimum value over the space of admissible functions. Moreover, this minimum value equals the yield strength $\tau$, and every minimizing function satisfies Equation~. The paper's stated purpose is to disprove this conjecture when $\ell/h>\sqrt{2}-1/2$ by showing that solutions to Equation~ cannot minimize the associated energy.
source_name: Jordan S. Cotler and Felipe Hernandez, “Resolution of a Conjecture in Nonlocal Strain-gradient Plasticity”, arXiv:1310.3426 (2014).

title: The centralizer conjecture for normal pairs of fusion systems
statement:
Let $((S,\mathcal{F}),(T,\mathcal{E}))$ be a normal pair of fusion systems realized by a normal pair $(G,H)$ of finite groups. Write $O_{p'}(H)$ for the largest normal subgroup of $H$ of order prime to $p$, and let $C_S(\mathcal{E})$ and $C_G(H)$ denote the corresponding centralizers. **Centralizer conjecture.** If $O_{p'}(H)=1$, then

$$
C_S(\mathcal{E})=C_G(H)\cap S.
$$

This is proposed as a fusion-system generalization of the $Z^*$-theorem. The source reports that attempts to construct a counterexample had failed, but the parser marks the conjecture as disproved; the nature of that disproof should be checked.

title: The maximum-point conjecture for maximal intersecting families
statement:
Let $N(k)$ denote the maximum number of points in a maximal intersecting family of $k$-sets. **Maximum-point conjecture.** For $k\geq 2$,

$$
N(k)=2k-2+\frac{1}{2}\binom{2k-2}{k-1}.
$$

Hanson and Toft proved the equality for $2\leq k\leq 4$. Tuza's constructions for $1$-critical uniform families do not disprove the conjecture because those families are not maximal intersecting families; the assertion remains open for general $k$.
source_name: Kaushik Majumder, “On the maximum number of points in a maximal intersecting family of finite sets”, arXiv:1402.7158 (2014).

title: Loehr–Warrington nonstandard $q$-binomial formula conjecture
statement:
Fix $a,b\in\mathbb{N}$. Let $\mathrm{R}(a,b)$ be the set of partitions fitting in the $b\times a$ rectangle, let $\mathsf{ml}_{b,a}(\mu)$ be the minimum level on the frontier of $\mu$, and let $h^+_{b,a}(\mu)$ and $h^-_{b,a}(\mu)$ be the corresponding arm–leg statistics. **Nonstandard $q$-binomial formula conjecture.**

$$
\genfrac{[}{]}{0pt}{}{a+b}{a,b}_q=\sum_{\mu\in\mathrm{R}(a,b)}q^{|\mu|+\mathsf{ml}_{b,a}(\mu)+h^+_{b,a}(\mu)}=\sum_{\mu\in\mathrm{R}(a,b)}q^{|\mu|+\mathsf{ml}_{b,a}(\mu)+h^-_{b,a}(\mu)}.
$$

This gives a proposed combinatorial interpretation of the $q$-binomial coefficient without a coprimality assumption; the supplied text does not state its resolution.

title: Maximality conjecture for a family of $p^k$-central spaces
statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, let $d=p^k$, and let $A=F[x,y]$ be a cyclic algebra of degree $d$. For some $0\leq e\leq k-1$, set

**Maximality conjecture.** The $p^k$-central space $V$ is maximal with respect to inclusion.

title: White's sharp Hausdorff-dimension conjecture for cone stratifications

title: The exact formula conjecture for the topological Tverberg threshold
statement:
Let $N_r(d)$ denote the least integer $N$ such that every continuous map from the $N$-simplex to $\mathbb{R}^d$ identifies points from $r$ pairwise disjoint faces. The parameters satisfy $r\ge 2$ and $d\ge 1$.

$$
N_r(d)=\begin{cases}(r-1)(d+1)&\text{if }r\text{ is a power of a prime or }d\le r,\\r(d+1)-1&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}
$$

This predicts the precise threshold governing the failure of the topological Tverberg phenomenon. The supplied text does not provide evidence resolving the conjecture.

title: The FJRW effective-algorithm conjecture for quintic singularities

\gamma\in(\boldsymbol{\mu}_5^{\mathrm{nar}})^{\times\ell},

title: Krattenthaler–Müller's two-row formula conjecture for NPS average complexity
statement:
Let $\lambda=(\lambda_1,\lambda_2)$ be a partition with two parts, and let $C(\lambda)$ denote the average number of exchanges performed by the Novelli–Pak–Stoyanovskii algorithm on a filling of shape $\lambda$. For $k\geq 0$, define the Pochhammer symbol by $(x)_0=1$ and $(x)_k=x(x+1)\cdots(x+k-1)$ for positive integers $k$.

**Krattenthaler–Müller's two-row formula conjecture.** The average case complexity is

$$
C(\lambda)=\frac{\lambda_1(\lambda_1-1)}{4}+\frac{\lambda_2(\lambda_2-3)}{4}-2\sum_{k=1}^{\lambda_2}\binom{\lambda_2}{k}\frac{(-1)^k(2k-2)!}{(\lambda_1-\lambda_2+2)_{2k-1}}.
$$

This is an exact formula for the average complexity when the partition has two parts. The source presents it as the third conjecture from private communication; no resolution is supplied here.

title: Width-minimizing positions that fail to minimize trunk or bridge number
statement: Let $K$ and $K'$ be knots, with embeddings $k$ and $k'$, respectively. title: General maximum-root bound for the mixed characteristic polynomial
statement:
Let $M_n(\mathbb{C})^{+}$ denote the positive semidefinite $n\times n$ complex matrices, and let a **positive contraction** be a positive semidefinite matrix bounded above by the identity. For $r\in\mathbb{N}\setminus\{1\}$, let $\chi_r[A]$ denote the $r$-characteristic polynomial of $A$, and let $\operatorname{max root}\chi_r[A]$ be its largest root. If $A\in M_n(\mathbb{C})^{+}$ is a positive contraction whose diagonal entries are all at most $\delta$, then **the mixed-determinant root bound conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{max root}\chi_r[A]\leq \frac{1}{r}\left(\sqrt{1-\delta}+\sqrt{(r-1)\delta}\right)^2.
$$

The text presents this as a plausible estimate for general $r$, following proved estimates for $r=2,3,4$; its resolution is not supplied here.

title: The outerplanar graph fractional-defect conjecture
statement:
A $2$-coloring assigns each vertex a red usage in $[0,1]$, with blue usage $1-r(v)$; the defect of a vertex is the sum, over its neighbors, of the overlap in their color usages, and $D(G,2)$ is the minimum possible maximum defect over all such colorings of $G$. **Outerplanar graph fractional-defect conjecture.** For any outerplanar graph $G$,

$$
D(G,2)<2.
$$

Ordinary $2$-colorings of outerplanar graphs have defect at most $2$, and the fan examples show that the minimum defect can approach $2$ from below. The conjecture asks whether the bound is always strictly improvable.

title: Piśniak's distinguishing-index conjecture for 2-connected graphs
statement:
Let $G$ be a simple connected graph. Its **distinguishing index** $D'(G)$ is the least number of labels in an edge labeling preserved only by the identity automorphism. Write $\Delta(G)$ for its maximum degree.

**Piśniak's conjecture.** If $G$ is a $2$-connected graph, then

$$
D'(G)\leq 1+\lceil \sqrt{\Delta(G)}\rceil.
$$

C(M,X;R,0,\ell,-\infty)=R\lvert\ell\rvert.

title: The minimum codegree conjecture for perfect matchings in $K_4^3$-free 3-graphs
statement:
Let $H$ be an $n$-vertex $3$-uniform hypergraph, where $n$ is sufficiently large and divisible by $3$. Write $\delta_2(H)$ for its minimum codegree, and let $K_4^3$ denote the complete $3$-uniform hypergraph on four vertices. A perfect matching is a collection of vertex-disjoint edges covering all vertices of $H$.

**$K_4^3$-free matching conjecture.** For any $\gamma>0$, for sufficiently large $n\in 3\mathbb{N}$, if $H$ contains no copy of $K_4^3$ and

$$
\delta_2(H)\geq \left(\frac{1}{3}+\gamma\right)n,
$$

then $H$ contains a perfect matching.

The examples preceding the conjecture show that the constant $1/3$ is a natural lower-bound barrier for the minimum codegree. The supplied source gives no information about whether the conjecture has been resolved.

title: Butterfly trace conjecture
statement:
Let $B$ be the butterfly poset on four elements $a,b,c,d$, with $a,b<_B c,d$. For a family $\mathcal F\subseteq 2^{[n]}$, let $Tr_{n-1}(n,B)$ denote the maximum size of a family whose traces on all $(n-1)$-subsets contain no copy of $B$. **Butterfly trace conjecture.** If $n\geq 5$, then

$$
Tr_{n-1}(n,B)=\binom{n}{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}.
$$

The paper proves the related exact formula $Tr(n,B)=\lfloor 3n/2\rfloor+1$, but the asserted value for traces on $(n-1)$-subsets is posed as an open problem.

title: Bergeron's positivity and unimodality conjecture for q-binomial differences
statement:
Let $a,b,c,d$ be positive integers such that $a$ is the smallest and $ad=bc$. The $q$-binomial coefficient is

$$
\binom{m+n}{m}_q=\frac{(1-q)(1-q^2)\cdots(1-q^{m+n})}{(1-q)(1-q^2)\cdots(1-q^m)\cdot(1-q)(1-q^2)\cdots(1-q^n)}.
$$

Thus $\binom{m+n}{m}_q$ is a symmetric polynomial in $q$. **Bergeron's positivity and unimodality conjecture.** The coefficients of the symmetric polynomial

$$
\binom{b+c}{b}_q-\binom{a+d}{d}_q
$$

are nonnegative and unimodal. This extends Bergeron's positivity problem, which asks whether these coefficients are always nonnegative. The conjecture is proved combinatorially in the cases $a\leq 3$ and $b,c\geq 4$; the general assertion remains open.
source_name: Fabrizio Zanello, “On Bergeron's positivity problem for q-binomial coefficients”, arXiv:1709.06187 (2018).

title: The conjecture that the minimum is attained at two copies of 2
statement:
For a fixed integer $p\geq4$, let $F_v(a_1,\ldots,a_s;q)$ denote the vertex Folkman number, and let $2_r$ denote $r$ occurrences of $2$. **The minimum-attainment conjecture.**

\min_{r\geq2}\left\{F_v(2_r,p;r+p-1)-r\right\}=F_v(2,2,p;p+1)-2,
$$

that is, $r'_0(p)=2$, and

$$
F_v(2_r,p;r+p-1)=F_v(2,2,p;p+1)+r-2,\qquad r\geq2.
$$

statement:
Let $n>1$ be an integer, and let $R=\mathbb{Z}_n$ be the ring of integers modulo $n$. The **modular Erdős–Burgess constant conjecture.**

title: Hamidoune's atom cardinality conjecture for torsion-free groups
statement: Let $G$ be a torsion-free group, let $C$ be a finite subset of $G$ containing the identity element, and let $n$ be a positive integer. title: Jones's conjecture on level-$(p,q)$ Furuta–Mahowald classes
statement:

q \geq \begin{cases} 2p+2 & p\equiv 1 \pmod 4,\\ 2p+2 & p\equiv 2 \pmod 4,\\ 2p+3 & p\equiv 3 \pmod 4,\\ 2p+4 & p\equiv 4 \pmod 4. \end{cases}
